title: The Two Dates on the Monument
title_ja: 記念碑に刻まれた二つの日付
fact_notes: 人物、場所、出来事、観察・実験の内容は架空の教材例。実在の研究結果や具体的なシステムの安全性を示すものではない。制作台帳は来歴確認用。

sentences.en: While preparing a local history presentation, Nao noticed two different dates on a monument standing near the town hall.
sentences.ja: 地域史の発表準備中、ナオは町役場近くの記念碑に異なる二つの日付があることに気づいた。

sentences.en: The larger date was easily visible from the main road, whereas the smaller one appeared on a plaque attached to the back.
sentences.ja: 大きな日付は大通りからよく見え、もう一方は裏面に取り付けられた銘板にあった。

sentences.en: Nao initially assumed that one of the dates had been recorded incorrectly.
sentences.ja: ナオは当初、どちらかの日付が誤って記録されたと思った。

sentences.en: Her history teacher advised her to investigate the purpose of each inscription before reaching a conclusion.
sentences.ja: 歴史教師は結論に至る前に各刻文の目的を調べるよう助言した。

sentences.en: At the town archive, Nao found an old announcement describing the event that the monument was intended to commemorate.
sentences.ja: 町の資料館で記念碑が記念することを意図した出来事を説明する古い告知を発見した。

sentences.en: The announcement contained the earlier of the two dates, but it did not mention the monument itself.
sentences.ja: 告知には二つのうち早い方の日付があったが記念碑自体への言及はなかった。

sentences.en: A photograph taken many years afterward showed residents gathering at the same location for an opening ceremony.
sentences.ja: 多年後の写真には同じ場所で除幕式に集まる住民が写っていた。

sentences.en: The caption dated that ceremony to the year recorded on the smaller plaque.
sentences.ja: 写真説明では式の年は小さな銘板に記録された年だった。

sentences.en: Nao realized that the two dates referred to different events rather than competing descriptions of the same event.
sentences.ja: 二つの日付は同じ出来事についての対立する記述でなく異なる出来事を示すと分かった。

sentences.en: She then wondered why the residents had decided to construct a monument so long after the original event.
sentences.ja: 住民がなぜ元の出来事のずっと後に記念碑を建てることにしたか疑問に思った。

sentences.en: Several surviving documents indicated that a local committee had organized the project and discussed various possible designs.
sentences.ja: 残る文書から地元の委員会が事業を企画し複数の設計案を検討していたと分かった。

sentences.en: However, the records did not establish whether every resident had supported the decision or shared the same interpretation of the past.
sentences.ja: しかし全住民が決定を支持し過去について同じ解釈を共有していたかまでは資料から分からなかった。

sentences.en: For her presentation, Nao created a timeline separating the original event from the later construction of the monument.
sentences.ja: 発表のため元の出来事と後の記念碑建設を分けた年表を作った。

sentences.en: She included quotations from the surviving documents and distinguished them from questions that remained unanswered.
sentences.ja: 残る文書からの引用を含め、未解決の問いと区別した。

sentences.en: Her classmates discussed how a monument could provide information about both an earlier event and the people who chose to remember it later.
sentences.ja: 記念碑は以前の出来事と後にそれを記憶することを選んだ人々の双方について情報を提供し得るとクラスで話し合った。

sentences.en: They suggested examining other memorials to consider how communities sometimes select particular aspects of their history for public attention.
sentences.ja: 地域が歴史の特定の側面に公の注目を集める方法を考えるため別の記念物も調べる提案が出た。

sentences.en: Nao learned that a historical object can belong to more than one period of history at the same time.
sentences.ja: 歴史的な物は同時に複数の時代に関係し得るとナオは学んだ。

sentences.en: Remembering an event is itself an action that takes place under specific social circumstances.
sentences.ja: 出来事を記憶すること自体が特定の社会的状況のもとで行われる行為である。

sentences.en: Studying both dates therefore offered a richer understanding than simply trying to decide which one was correct.
sentences.ja: したがって両方の日付を調べることはどちらが正しいかだけを決めようとするより豊かな理解をもたらした。

sentences.en: The apparent contradiction on the monument had become an opportunity to distinguish the past from the later interpretation of it.
sentences.ja: 記念碑の一見矛盾した記述は過去と後世の解釈を区別する機会となった。

questions.prompt: What did Nao notice on the monument?
options: A modern map of the town.
Both dates referred to the opening ceremony.
The monument had no historical value.
The dates had been added that morning.
questions.explanation_ja: 一方の日付が誤りだと思った。

questions.prompt: What did the old announcement describe?
options: The event commemorated by the monument.
Every detail of the monument's construction.
questions.explanation_ja: 記念碑が記念する元の出来事。

questions.prompt: What showed a later opening ceremony?
options: A photograph from many years afterward.

questions.prompt: What resolved the apparent conflict between the dates?
options: The smaller date was a printing error.
They referred to different historical events.
The larger date was invented by Nao.
Neither date appeared in any document.
questions.explanation_ja: 異なる出来事を示していた。

questions.prompt: What did the surviving documents not establish?
options: Whether there had been discussions about designs.
Whether the original event was commemorated.
Whether all residents supported the decision.
questions.explanation_ja: 全住民の支持は確定できなかった。

questions.prompt: What did Nao create for her presentation?
options: A fictional date to fill the gap.
A timeline distinguishing the two events.
A list of all town residents.
questions.explanation_ja: 元の出来事と建設を分けた年表。

questions.prompt: What can memorials reveal about later generations?
options: Which aspects of the past they chose to emphasize publicly.
That every community remembers all events equally.
That every historical interpretation is identical.
That later generations never make choices about history.
questions.explanation_ja: 何を公に記憶するかの選択を示す。
一見そのように見える。

options: Only the earliest date on an object matters.
Historical objects may reveal both earlier events and later acts of remembrance.
All historical objects belong to one period only.
questions.explanation_ja: 元の出来事と後世の記憶行為を読み取る。

grammar.focus: that the monument was intended to commemorate
grammar.explanation_ja: thatはeventを修飾し、be intended toは〜する目的。

grammar.focus: whether every resident had supported the decision
grammar.explanation_ja: whether節は確定できなかった内容を表す。

grammar.focus: more than one period of history
grammar.explanation_ja: more than oneは複数の時期を指す。

paraphrases.explanation_ja: 記念碑が記念する出来事を示す告知を発見。

paraphrases.explanation_ja: 複数時代に関係し得る。
